### P74 (6e0313eee, 8eb1d6b1e, d15c6066c) perf(runtime): answer a plain object's absent named read from its shape
- Area / platform: named and computed property reads (`perry-runtime/src/object/native_get.rs`, `shapes_own_data.rs`, `field_get_set/accessors.rs`, `field_get_set/get_field_by_name.rs`) / all targets; measured on wasm32 and x86_64.
- Problem: a read that does not hit the inline cache pays the full generic lookup, and an absent key pays the most: it walks to `Object.prototype` and then probes accessor, getter and brand surfaces that a plain object cannot have. ajv's generated validators, find-my-way, lru-cache and fastify read many absent keys (`n.pattern`, `v.then`, `v.toJSON`, `v.nodeType`) from one site that sees many shapes, so the site stays megamorphic and every read takes the miss path. The Storage cold start spends 577 ms inclusive in `js_object_get_field_slow`, most of it in JS getter bodies.
- Root cause: (1) the inherited walk read `Object.prototype` through the generic by-name path although its own data fields come from its shape. (2) The by-name path had a data-only lookup for hits, but a definite miss still fell through to the whole accessor/getter machinery, even for a receiver that provably has no surface beyond its shape. (3) Perry lowers a closed-shape object literal, `{}` included, to `new __AnonShape_<hash>()`: a synthetic class instance with a nonzero class id and no registered name. A gate written for class-less receivers never saw a compiled literal.
- Fix: (1) `object_prototype_data_read` reads `Object.prototype`'s own data field from its shape in both branches of `default_object_prototype_property_value`, and declines when the receiver is `Object.prototype` itself. (2) `try_settled_get_by_name` returns undefined for a definite data miss when `plain_receiver_miss_is_final` also holds: the object is in the ordinary heap, not forwarded and an ordinary object, with no dictionary or overflow store, no meta flags, a shape of kind `Ordinary`, no brands, a `proto_id` of default or null with no recorded prototype link, and either no class (birth-marked plain) or a nonzero class id that `class_id_admissible` accepts: an anon-shape id with an empty class identity (no name, no methods, no accessors, no statics). That predicate is memoized by the property-plan semantic epoch, so a class that later gains a surface retires settling at once. Getters, setters, proxies, prototype mutation, deletes, symbol keys and numeric-string keys all take the generic path unchanged.
- Test: wasi probes `.github/supa/wasi-probes/dynamic-get-matrix.js` (about 100 lines compared with node: own and inherited data, absent keys ending at `Object.prototype` or a null prototype, accessors, `Object.prototype` additions and removals after a miss, shadows and deletes, prototype swaps, symbol and numeric-string keys, `Object.keys` order, dictionary-sized objects, class instances, arrays, functions, RegExp, boxed primitives, built-ins) and `dynamic-get-bench.js` (checksums compared with node, ns per read on stderr). Unit tests in `object/native_get/tests.rs`: the settled lookup matches the generic one across a key matrix for plain, marked, anon-shape, accessor-bearing and prototyped receivers, and an anon-shape literal settles until its class gains a surface. Test-only commits: `692845d94` makes the closure-allocation counter per-thread, which fixes the flaky `descriptor_snapshot_named_array_accessors_copy_in_each_rebind_window` (a global counter raced with other tests); `5242c2d77` and `4d85b755c` trim and extend the probes.
- Measured (CI, x86_64 Blacksmith, `dynamic-get-bench`, best of 3, N = 200000, same host per column pair; runs 39214371584 base, 39214368393 with `f639c86ad`+`7d350aaec`, 39214361277 and 39214364922 with `0535a8938`): total 3650 -> 3112 -> 1215 ms (1222 on the repeat). Named reads from a megamorphic site 827 -> 681 -> 175 ns/read (`named-megamorphic`), probes on any value 706 -> 591 -> 180 ns/read (`named-probe-any`), small objects with absent keys 642 -> 547 -> 230 ns/read, an absent key ending at `Object.prototype` 780 -> 705 -> 367 ns/read, a 400-key dictionary 641 -> 554 -> 242 ns/read, a three-link chain 582 -> 542 -> 383 ns/read. Item (1) is worth -15% of the total; item (2) with the anon-shape admission of item (3) worth a further -61% (`0535a8938`). `7d350aaec` alone gave nothing until the admission landed: a counter run showed its gate never true for a compiled literal. Storage on wasm (run 39216892926 and 39216896716 against the unpatched module run in the same smoke job, baseline run 39192203548 as the reference): ready 3800 -> 3396 and 3776 -> 3355 ms (-10.6%, -11.1%), 5 MB case 3915 -> 3659 and 3796 -> 3423; with `f639c86ad` alone it was -3% (3812 -> 3696). Storage native (x86_64): ready 1617 and 1803 ms against 1651-1794 ms before, no measurable change.
- Not fixed, found on the way: misses on an instance of a declared class (1430 ns/read in `class-instance`), on a dictionary-mode or overflow receiver and on a function are not settled; a RegExp `.flags` getter costs about 108 ms in the Storage profile. The matrix leaves out three divergences from node that this work did not touch: `__proto__` of a plain function answers an object, not `Function.prototype`; `Map`, `Set` and `Promise` computed-key reads do not resolve inherited names; a symbol added to `Object.prototype` is invisible to an inheriting plain object. `array::element_shape::tests::prototype_writes_keep_proofs_and_an_instance_relink_retires_them` already fails on the base (`element_shape_tests.rs:398`).
- Upstream: not cherry-picked. Depends on: none. PR-AY.
- Merge of upstream `f07e51ebf` (2026-10-19): kept. `object/native_get.rs` is not touched by any commit of this window, so the settled-miss code is as it was and the `object::native_get::tests` suite passes on the merged tree (single-threaded, as `regressions.sh` runs the runtime tests). `dynamic-get-matrix.js` and `regexp-flags-latch.js` run in `wasi-linux`.

### P75 04bb656ae fix(runtime): resolve a grown array's forwarding stub in the remaining consumers
- Area / platform: the array arms of `format_jsvalue` and `format_jsvalue_for_json` (`builtins/formatting.rs`: `console.log`, `util.inspect`, `%o`), `util_format_json_array_has_cycle` (`formatting/util_format.rs`: `util.format('%j')`), the `console.table` readers (`builtins/table.rs`) and the child_process argument lists (`child_process/value_util.rs`, `registry.rs`: `spawn`, `spawnSync`, `execFile*`, detached spawn) / all targets.
- Problem: P64 showed that a list grown by push through a longer path (`this.a.b.push(v)`), through a parameter, or on an object field appended across timer ticks leaves a forwarding stub (#233) in the stale binding, and that `Buffer.concat` read it raw. This audit looked for every other place in `perry-runtime` and `perry-stdlib` that reads an `ArrayHeader` or its elements without resolving forwarding, and probed each candidate with those shapes against node.
- Root cause: the same as P64. The consumers above stripped the NaN-box tag and read `length` and the elements raw, so a stale head made `util.inspect`, `console.table` and `%j` trap on wasm32 (out-of-bounds read at the new address), and `spawnSync` / `spawn` hang or crash on native (the length word is the new address).
- Fix: each site resolves the list with the existing `crate::array::clean_arr_ptr` (or `clean_arr_ptr_mut`, `js_array_get_f64`) and treats a null result as empty. No new helper.
- Test: one probe per consumer, because a failing consumer aborts the run and would hide the rest. wasi probes `stale-array-inspect.js`, `stale-array-inspect-nested.js`, `stale-array-format-json.js`, `stale-array-table.js`; native probes `stale-array-spawnsync-native.js`, `stale-array-spawn-native.js`, `stale-array-execfilesync-native.js` (`// compare-node`). Each runs a fresh copy, a nested-field list and a list grown through a parameter. Before the fix (run 39217267733 for wasi, 39214146697 for native) every wasi probe trapped (exit 134) and spawnSync and spawn failed (exit 124 and 139); after it (runs 39217271271 and 39214151022) they pass. `stale-array-consumers.js` holds controls for the consumers that already follow forwarding (JSON, Buffer, TypedArray, Set, Map, apply and spread, Reflect, Promise combinators, fs.writevSync); it passes on both. `execFileSync` is intermittent before the fix: it hung in one run (39213389326) and passed in another (39214146697), so its probe is a regression guard, not a proof.
- Audited and already safe: TypedArray constructor and `set`, `Buffer.from` and `buffer.set`, `js_closure_call_apply_with_spread` and `js_method_call_value_apply` (`apply`, spread), `JSON.stringify` with and without a replacer or indent, `Set`, `Map`, `Object.fromEntries`, `String.fromCharCode.apply`, `Reflect.apply` and `construct`, `Promise.all` / `allSettled` / `race` / `any`, `fs.writevSync`, `URLSearchParams`, dynamic indexing, `param_type_guard`, `js_array_clone`, `v8.serialize` (resolves through `js_array_from_value`). Not applicable (arrays the runtime builds itself): rest-argument arrays, key and attribute lists, GC and internal arrays.
- Not fixed, not confirmed: `estimate_json_size` (`json/stringify.rs`, root replacer path) and `format_error_array` (`formatting/errors.rs`) read the header raw but their probes passed before any fix (`JSON.stringify(stale, fn)` printed the right text; `util.inspect(new AggregateError(stale))` matched), so they were left alone; `write_dense_array` in `child_process/v8_serde.rs` has a second caller with a raw pointer, unreachable from `v8.serialize` of an array; `perry-stdlib/src/sqlite/better.rs` `params_from_array` reads a bound-parameter list raw (`clean_arr_ptr` is `pub(crate)` in perry-runtime, and the module is not reachable under wasip1, so it has no probe); `promise/async_step.rs` `array_value_ptr` reads `length` raw for `Array.fromAsync` (a real array does not reach it); `json/reviver.rs` `annotate_source_tree` and `js_array_print` read arrays the runtime just built.
- Found, not fixed: `console.log` of an array of more than six elements groups its columns differently from node even for a fresh list (strings print several per line where node prints one per line when they are wide; numbers are padded to a different width; an object holding such an array prints it on one line). This is why the probes compare `util.inspect` of the stale list with `util.inspect` of a copy instead of the printed layout.
- Upstream: not cherry-picked. Depends on: none. PR-AZ.
### P76 07cd5f7bd, 0b1dc6a83, f59841774, 04cb22876, 2e4d602c4 perf(runtime): pace large-buffer fulls by heap growth and live size
- Area / platform: `gc/allocation_pacing.rs` (`due_arm`, the large band), `gc/policy.rs`, `gc/cycle.rs`, `gc/telemetry.rs` (`PERRY_GC_LOG`, pid) / all targets; measured on wasm32.
- Problem: a warm Storage request ran a full mark-sweep about every second request (run A 39196702970 and run B, same module: 22 fulls over 45 warm requests, 1.59 to 1.73 s of GC in a 6 s run, 50 to 60 ms per full). Uploads regressed the same way (1 MB PUT 29/66 ms on the old module, 51/98 ms on x86_64/arm64): the extra time is the same full-GC cadence plus about 23 ms of first-hit lazy schema compile (Storage, not Perry).
- Root cause: a native buffer over 4096 bytes is a `ForeignBuffer` cell born in the old generation, with its bytes counted as external. Minors never see it, so only a full sweep frees a dead one, and every 1 MiB buffer is a candidate for "burst-large" debt. Three things made it fire per request. (1) The large band was a flat 32 MiB (`LARGE_BAND_FLOOR`) however large the live heap was, so a 25 MB old heap paid one 55 to 68 ms full (about 3 ms per MiB of live heap on WASI) per 32 MiB of buffers. (2) A burst full was owed whether or not the mature heap had grown since the last one (`burst_unpaid_at_full`), so a loop of dead buffers owed one each time the band filled. (3) `PERRY_GC_TRACE` panicked on `std::process::id` under WASI, so none of this was observable.
- Fix: (1) `large_band = LARGE_BAND_FLOOR.max(live_after_full)`: the debt allowed before a large-birth full scales with the live heap, so the amortised cost of a full per allocated byte stays bounded as the heap grows, and memory stays at most the floor plus one live heap of dead buffers. (2) `due_arm` owes a burst full only when the old heap has grown past what the last full left. (3) the trace record takes its pid from `os::current_process_id()`, which is 0 on wasi (P71 added the helper; the branch's own copy of it was dropped). `PERRY_GC_LOG=1` prints one line per finished collection (kind, trigger, arm, pause, freed, old bytes, external bytes, root-stack depths) and one `owed arm=` line per full, which is how the rest was found.
- Test: wasi probe `.github/supa/wasi-probes/gc-request-buffers.js` (120 requests, each reads 1 MiB, concatenates and copies it, plus about 1 MB of small garbage, over a 60,000-object live heap; stdout is compared with node, stderr must hold at most 16 `kind=full` lines, RSS under 600 MB; measured 11 fulls, peak RSS 401 MB). The unit tests in `gc/tests/allocation_pacing.rs` follow the new band (`BURST_BUFFERS = 9`).
- Measured (run 39226213653, same host, base module = run 39192203548): warm median ms, base to new: get_6mb 128.2 to 65.9, put_6mb 174.2 to 107.5, get_1mb 26.1 to 27.0, put_1mb 56.3 to 58.6 (within noise); ready_ms 3941 to 3777; RSS idle 367 to 370 MB, after the warm requests 401 to 415 MB. The base module has no log, so its collection counts come from runs A/B (same module as the pre-fix new module): 22 fulls and 1.59 to 1.73 s of GC over the whole warm sequence; with the fix the sequence logs 8 fulls and 0.75 s. Small requests are not faster because a full is still owed per 32 MiB of buffers, and 1 MiB requests pay it at about 1 in 10.
- Not fixed, found on the way: (a) The full collector force-marks every object in the last five 1 MiB arena blocks (`BLOCK_PERSIST_WINDOW`, block persistence, which protects values only a register or wasm local holds; the conservative stack scan is off on wasm, so it runs on every full). A program that allocates almost nothing but big buffers therefore keeps their small holders, and through them the buffers' bytes, alive until the window moves on: the same loop without the small garbage retained all 360 MB it allocated and peaked at 531 MB. Measured by diagnostic runs: the holders are nursery arrays marked with no heap or root holder, `bpforce` (the force-mark counter) was 2056 per full, and adding 20,000 small objects per request freed every buffer (ext 0 after each full). A server allocates far more than 5 MB between requests, so the retention is bounded in practice, but the bound is in allocation volume, not bytes. A real fix needs either an alloc-epoch window or finalising young native buffers in minors (they are born old, so minors never free them), both larger than this patch. (b) A separate old-reclaim trigger (`gc_old_reclaim_growth_band_bytes`, 32 MiB or baseline over a divisor) can start a full independently of the large band; the two overlap for buffer-heavy programs. (c) `std::process::id` is still called by `function_order`, `update_notify` and `bun_ffi`; none is on a WASI path today.
- Upstream: not cherry-picked. Depends on: none. PR-BA.

### P77 (b80be3679, eb22f4d5c, 927a217a1, f0cedb024) perf(runtime): settle inherited misses on declared-class instances and read RegExp flags from the bits
- Area / platform: named reads on class instances (`perry-runtime/src/object/native_get.rs`, `object/native_call_method/class_holder.rs`, `object/class_value.rs`) and RegExp flag reads (`regex/instance.rs`, `regex/perex_match_search.rs`, `object/regex_read_sites.rs`) / all targets; measured on wasm32 and x86_64.
- Problem: (1) P74 settled a plain object's absent named read from its shape but declined every declared-class instance, so `instance[key]` for an absent key or an `Object.prototype` name still paid the whole generic lookup (1451 ns/read in the `class-instance` phase of `dynamic-get-bench`). (2) `.flags` and the flag-driven internals of replace, match, split and matchAll cost about 108 ms in the Storage cold profile: both took the slow generic read whenever `RegExp.prototype` had been written to at all.
- Root cause: (1) the generic read of a class instance consults, after the own keys, the class's accessors, its prototype registrations, a per-instance prototype, an evaluation's pinned heritage and then `Object.prototype`. For a chain of purely compiled declared classes every one of those answers from a holder's shape, but nothing exposed that, so the gate in `try_data_lookup_key` simply declined. (2) The RegExp builtin fact (`regex::instance::builtin`) bundled the receiver's birth layout with the `RegExp.prototype` shadow bit, which flips on any write to the prototype, even one that leaves the nine flag accessors untouched.
- Fix: (1) `class_instance_inherited_read` walks the holder chain with `chain_method_admitting` (the existing class-holder walk, now generic over the admission test) and answers undefined when neither the instance nor any holder lists the name, or the `Object.prototype` data value when only it does. It admits only compiled classes (below `FIRST_RUNTIME_CLASS_ID`), no relinked, runtime or native parent, no overriding `class_prototype_object`, no pinned constructing class, no recorded per-instance prototype. Members, accessors, `constructor`, `__proto__`, `@@` and `#` keys decline. The walk reads live shapes, so nothing is cached and the existing epoch and class-surface invalidation needs no new hook: a method, accessor or data property added to any holder, a relinked holder or instance, or a change to `Object.prototype` changes what it reads. (2) `regex::instance::birth_layout` splits the layout test out of `builtin`. `regex_read_sites::flag_getters` holds while the receiver has the birth layout and all nine flag accessors on `RegExp.prototype` are still the builtin getter thunks (memoized by the property-plan semantic epoch and the prototype's shape stamp); `perex_match_search::match_flags` and `.flags` use it, so an unrelated write to `RegExp.prototype` no longer retires them, and a redefined or deleted flag getter does.
- Test: wasi probes `.github/supa/wasi-probes/dynamic-get-matrix.js` (class section, about 60 comparisons with node: base, subclass and unrelated instances, statics, a method, a data property and a getter added to a class prototype after reads settled and then removed, an `Object.prototype` property added, shadowed and removed, own shadows, `Object.setPrototypeOf` and `__proto__` on instances and on class prototypes (including null), a frozen prototype, a class with a private field and accessor, `extends null`, `extends Array`, `extends Error`, a class expression, per-evaluation classes) and `regexp-flags-latch.js` (all flags and the string methods after an unrelated prototype write, a redefined, deleted or data-turned flag getter, own `flags` and `global`, subclasses with their own getters, a swapped prototype, `lastIndex`). The probe lines that depend on whether the engine reads `flags` or the individual getters inside replace and match differ between node versions and are left out. Unit tests: `object/native_get/tests.rs` (settled class read equals the generic read across a key matrix, retires on a method, accessor, relink and per-instance prototype), `object/regex_builtin_shape_tests.rs` (flag fact holds after an unrelated write, fails after an accessor redefine).
- Measured (CI, x86_64 Blacksmith, `dynamic-get-bench`, best of 3, N = 200000; run 39219095386 is the P74 head `0384aed72`, run 39235497499 is this branch): `class-instance` 1451 -> 528 ns/read (290.3 -> 105.7 ms); total 1224.7 -> 1060.1 ms; every other phase unchanged within 3 ns (`named-megamorphic` 174 -> 181, `small-hit/miss` 231 -> 237). The remaining 528 ns is the two method keys of the seven in the phase (`run`, `stop`): a class method hit still takes the generic path, because answering it needs the method's function object. Storage on wasm, same host and same tree (supa/storage-opt `614863a6c` plus the branch under test, baseline module run 39216179103, `new_100k` / `new_5mb` / `new_gc` ready in ms): P74 alone (run 39235502513) 1563 -> 1390, 1656 -> 1626, 1623 -> 1530; P74 plus P77 (run 39229517620) 1631 -> 1448, 1562 -> 1572, 1613 -> 1483; RSS idle 303 MB in both, after 343-365 MB. P77 alone does not show in the Storage numbers (the difference between the two runs is inside the 60 ms run-to-run spread), so the RegExp half is unproven at that level: it was written against the profile's `match_flags` and `.flags` frames, the cause (a write to `RegExp.prototype` that leaves the accessors builtin) is a hypothesis, and a fresh cold profile is the check.
- Test-only fixes in this slice: `array::element_shape::tests::prototype_writes_keep_proofs_and_an_instance_relink_retires_them` (the P74 note) was a wrong test, not a runtime bug: the first prototype write in a process materializes `globalThis`, which relinks the builtin prototype tower and retires every element-shape proof conservatively; the test now materializes `globalThis` first and says why. Three more tests raced on process-global state and are now deterministic: `classless_function_store_records_a_shape_plan` and the two `class_chain_tojson_memo_*` tests depended on the process-wide property-plan epochs staying still (`97e9664d4` -> `62f7611a7` counts both epochs per thread in test builds and restores their exact assertions), `spec_and_generic_push_entries_*` read a global probe counter that parallel tests bumped (now a test-only thread-local in `value/addr_class.rs`), and `arguments_objects_of_one_arity_share_one_shape` read the process-global ShapeId allocator (`ed9a251eb` -> `04030e448` counts ids minted by the calling thread).
- Not fixed, found on the way: a class method or class-held data hit on an instance is not settled; a `class X extends Map` instance answers undefined for `size`, `get` and `toString` through a computed key (a native parent declines the settled path, and the generic path does not resolve them either); exec and test still decline the aggregate RegExp fact after any prototype write (`builtin_exec_data`, about 22 samples).
- Upstream: not cherry-picked. Depends on: P74 (the settled miss and `plain_receiver_miss_is_final`). PR-BB.
- Merge of upstream `f07e51ebf` (2026-10-19): kept. `object/native_call_method/class_holder.rs` is not touched by any commit of this window; `class_instance_inherited_read` and the `class_holder` and `object::native_get::tests` selections pass on the merged tree. Upstream `390be8c40` rewrote `array::element_shape::tests::prototype_writes_keep_proofs_and_an_instance_relink_retires_them` (it registers the class and materializes its prototype before the arrays acquire proofs); that conflicted with this patch's `js_get_global_this()` pre-pay and upstream's version was taken. It passes.

### P78 (this commit) fix(runtime): keep the block-persistence window under a Scan decision where the scan does nothing
- Area / platform: GC block persistence (`gc/cycle.rs` `block_persistence_is_redundant`, `gc/roots/scan_mode.rs` `conservative_scan_is_effective`) / wasm32-wasip1; native behaviour is unchanged.
- Problem: pre-existing and latent. `block_persistence_is_redundant` answered true for any `ConservativeStackScanDecision::Scan`, on the grounds that the scan had pinned every register-held object. `mark_stack_roots_unchecked` walks the stack only on x86_64 and aarch64, so on wasm32 a `Scan` pins nothing, and the collections that run under a pinned `ManualGcScanGuard::force_full_scan` (the nursery slack valve, the alloc-point old-reclaim valve, emergency reclaim, `perry/gc` `minor()`, or `PERRY_CONSERVATIVE_STACK_SCAN=full`) dropped the window that protects an unrooted runtime-helper local. Storage is not affected in practice: its event-loop fulls log `frame=0 window=0` (they begin at a declared safepoint) and the valves did not fire in the smoke runs.
- Root cause: the shortcut conflated "the scan was requested" with "the scan ran".
- Fix: one predicate, `roots::conservative_scan_is_effective()` (`cfg!(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64"))`, with a `cfg(test)` override), and the `Scan` shortcut requires it. The other `Scan` readers are not the same bug: `copying.rs` `evaluate_with_stack_decision` and `cycle.rs` `pin_currently_marked_as_conservative` treat `Scan` as a reason to be more conservative (no copying minor, pin what the scan marked), and `policy.rs` `contract_scan_heal_guard` returns early on `Scan` but is already inert without native stack maps. `PERRY_GC_DIAG=1` now prints one `[gc-block-persist]` line per collection (`scan`, `effective`, `frame`, `ran`, trigger and the cumulative force-mark count `window=`); `block_persist_force_mark_count` is no longer test-only.
- Test: gc test `gc::tests::block_persist_scan_window` (a full under a pinned `Scan` with an active shadow frame force-marks the window when the scan is ineffective, and still skips it when effective; the first fails without the fix), wasi probe `gc-valve-retained-window.js` (`Array.from({ length: 3e6 }, ...)` retains more than 64 MB inside one synchronous call, output compared with node, asserts the `PERRY_GC_DIAG` line `scan=1 effective=0 frame=1 ran=1`; on CI an `ArenaBytes` valve full logged it with `window=46810`). Found on the way, not fixed: `new Array(3e6).fill(0)` followed by 3e6 object stores, or `.fill(0).map(...)` at 3e6, traps out of bounds in `js_array_fill` on wasm32 (access 32 bytes past the end of a 14.6 MB linear memory), so the probe builds its array with `Array.from`.
- Upstream: not cherry-picked (written on the fork). Depends on: none. PR-BC, a candidate for upstream PerryTS/perry.

### P79 5138da942 fix(runtime): read a native alias's state through an unmarked ordinary receiver
- Area / platform: `listed` and the `inherited_walk` absence proof in `object/layout_probe.rs` / all targets.
- Problem: `function Res(req) { http.ServerResponse.call(this, req) }; util.inherits(Res, http.ServerResponse); new Res(req).socket` (and any other name the aliased handle owns) read as `undefined` once the front-end layout probe answered the read. The lib test `inline_cache_reads_native_alias_state_without_caching_a_miss` failed on the base with `left: NaN right: 41.0`; it had been recorded as a macOS-only failure and is not platform-specific.
- Root cause: `register_this_to_handle_alias` records the alias in the `OBJECT_META_FLAG_NATIVE_ALIAS` meta flag. Only a receiver born with `OBJ_FLAG_PLAIN_ORDINARY` takes the `OrdinaryNativeAlias` shape kind (`receiver_ordinary_kind`); `new F()` allocates with `js_object_alloc(0, 0)`, which is unmarked, so it stays `OrdinaryUnmarked`. The unmarked arms of `listed` and `inherited_walk` only checked `OBJECT_META_FLAG_EXOTIC_READ_RECEIVER` before treating an unlisted key as a proven miss, so the read never reached `alias_forward_property_read`.
- Fix: both arms also refuse an object whose meta has `OBJECT_META_FLAG_NATIVE_ALIAS`, the way they already refuse an exotic read receiver; the read then takes the slow path that forwards to the handle.
- Test: wasi probe `native-alias-unmarked-read.js` (reads `socket`, `connection`, `listening` and header state of an aliased `Server` and `ServerResponse`, compared with node); the lib test above, added to `regressions.sh`.
- Upstream: not cherry-picked. Depends on: none. PR-BD.
- Merge of upstream `f07e51ebf` (2026-10-19): kept as it was. `de632eeb8` (seeding the flagless colour index twice adds nothing) and `d9481ba04` (coloured stores take F64 lanes) edit other hunks of `object/layout_probe.rs`; this patch's native-alias read is intact and the merge was textually clean.
- Merge of upstream `647b60de8` (2026-10-20): kept. Upstream `c39e81fe1` changed `object/layout_probe.rs`; the P79 hunks (`listed`, `inherited_walk`) are intact in the merged result.

### P80 300aee6e5, c56c8d152, 11243a36e fix(runtime): treat a pre-sized array's slots past its backing store as holes in fill, copyWithin, flat and the for-of record read
- Area / platform: `js_array_fill` and `js_array_fill_range` (`array/concat_reverse.rs`), `js_array_copy_within` (`array/immutable.rs`), `js_array_flat` and `js_array_flat_into` (`array/flat_clone.rs`), the compact `for...of` record read and step (`lower_record_index`, `lower_record_next` in `expr/index_get/guarded_array.rs`) / all targets.
- Problem: `new Array(3e6).fill(0)` followed by 3e6 object stores, and `new Array(3e6).fill(0).map((_, i) => ({ i, s: [i] }))`, trapped on wasm32 inside `js_array_fill` (an access 32 bytes past a 14.6 MB linear memory). On native the same write corrupts the neighbouring heap or faults at a block end (the unit test SIGSEGVs without the fix).
- Root cause: above `MAX_FRESH_DENSE_ARRAY_LENGTH` (1,000,000) `new Array(n)` is `js_array_alloc(0)` (capacity 4) with a logical `length = n`; indexed reads treat a slot at or past capacity as a hole (`array_truncate_length`). `fill` looped `0..length` (and `fill(v, s, e)` over `s..e`) storing `*elements.add(i)` with no capacity check, so every store past the 4-slot store landed outside the allocation. The same assumption "length bounds the allocation" was found in three consumers: `copyWithin` (memmove over `[s, e)`), `flat` / `flat_into` (read `0..length` raw, yielding garbage elements and a wrong length) and the codegen record read/step used by `for...of` over an array, which loaded the slot after checking only the length (a string-tagged garbage value reached `js_string_addref_if_heap_string` and trapped).
- Fix: a `fill_slots` helper grows the array to `end` before writing (`js_array_grow`, value rooted, old head left as a forwarding stub) unless the range starts more than `DENSE_ARRAY_GAP_LIMIT` (1024) past the store and is shorter than the gap or the array has sparse index properties, in which case it stores through `js_array_set_f64_extend`. The codegen `fill` arms write the grown head back to the local, capture or global (`emit_grow_mutator_writeback`, as `push` and `unshift` do). `copyWithin` takes its existing per-index spec loop when `length > capacity`; `flat` stops at the store (slots past it are holes); the record read and step compare the index with the capacity and send an unbacked slot to the cold dispatcher, which answers a hole.
- Test: wasi probes `array-fill-presized.js` (fill and fill(v, s, e) across the growth thresholds, with ranges inside, crossing and far past the store, then read, map, push and fill again), `array-fill-3m-objects.js` (the 3e6 case, both shapes) and `array-presized-reads.js` (an unfilled array read through forEach, map, filter, join, reverse, sort, for...of, keys, entries, some, every, find, reduce, slice, concat, spread, Array.from, copyWithin, splice, shift, unshift, length changes, JSON and flat); each is compared with node. Unit tests `large_presized_tests::fill*` (fill covers a 1.2M array and the old head forwards; fill_range grows for a crossing range and stays sparse for a far short one).
- Not changed: the bounded-index tier (`lower_bounded_array_index_get_checked`) and the packed-loop tiers also load a slot after a length-only check, but no probe reached them over capacity (index loops over an unfilled 1.2M array passed before any change there), so they were left alone. `Object.keys` skips the dense indices of an array above 100000 elements, so the probes digest at a stride.
- Upstream: not cherry-picked. Depends on: none. PR-BE.

### P81 1e21b047c fix(stdlib,codegen): declare js_ext_net_socket_on with the i64 return its definition has
- Area / platform: the `extern "C"` block in `perry-stdlib/src/common/wrapper_imports.rs` (and its one call in `common/dispatch/fastify_net.rs`), the declaration in `perry-codegen/src/runtime_decls/stdlib_ffi/language_core.rs` / wasm32 (native targets do not check extern signatures).
- Problem: linking the wasm32 runtime without LTO (the `regress-wasi` fast build profile, `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=off`, codegen-units 16) failed in `wasm-ld` with `function signature mismatch: js_ext_net_socket_on`. The release profile (thin LTO, one codegen unit) links the same sources.
- Root cause: `js_ext_net_socket_on` in `perry-ext-net/src/payload_abi.rs` is `fn(i64, i64, i64) -> i64` (it returns the handle for chaining, like `js_ext_net_socket_once`), while `perry-stdlib` declared it with no return and the codegen declaration used `VOID`. Native linkers resolve by name only, and under LTO the wasm backend only sees the callee's real type after inlining and so never compared the two. `wasm32/runtime_abi.tsv` already had the right row (`i64`, generated from the definition).
- Fix: both declarations return `i64`; the stdlib call site discards the result explicitly (the dispatch arm returns the handle itself). No lowering emits a call to the symbol, so no codegen call site changes.
- Test: none of its own. The mismatch is a link error, so every wasm32 runtime build without LTO (`regress-wasi` with `fast_build` auto or on) is the test. A wasi probe cannot reach it: the call sits in the net-socket dispatch arm, which wasi has no sockets to drive.
- Same-kind audit: a script comparing every `extern "C"` block declaration in `crates/` with the matching definition (arity, float vs integer, void vs value, integer width; unions of pointer/usize/i64 treated as equal, UI crates and force-link stubs skipped) found no other mismatch between stdlib/ext/runtime Rust declarations. `scripts/runtime_abi_check.py` reports 66 codegen-side `ret_ignored` entries (codegen declares void over an `i32`-returning runtime function, mostly `js_fs_*_sync`); `wasm32/abi_adapt.rs` adapts those calls from the table, and none is a link-time mismatch.
- Upstream: not cherry-picked. Depends on: none. PR-BF, a candidate for upstream PerryTS/perry.

### P82 (this commit) fix(codegen): write fill's grown head back only to a binding the arguments left alone
- Area / platform: the `fill` arms of `lower_array_method` (`perry-codegen/src/lower_array_method.rs`) / all targets.
- Problem: `let a = [1, 2]; a.fill((a = [9], 0)); console.log(a)` printed the filled original `[ 0, 0 ]` where node prints `[ 9 ]`. The same for a pre-sized array past one million elements (where `fill` grows the store and replaces the head) and for `start`/`end` arguments that rebind the receiver's variable.
- Root cause: P80 made `fill` write the head it returns back into a single-local receiver (`fill_writeback`), because a grown array leaves a forwarding stub and a boxed or captured local never follows it. The write-back ran after the arguments, unconditionally, so it overwrote an assignment the arguments had made.
- Fix: the arm decides the write-back AFTER the call (`emit_fill_with_writeback`). It roots the receiver in a temp-root slot before the call, and after it compares the rooted receiver re-read with a fresh read of the binding; the write-back is emitted behind that `i1` (`fill.writeback` / `fill.writeback_done` blocks). A collection during the call rewrites the binding's root and the slot alike, so an untouched binding still compares equal; a grown array's binding keeps the old head bits (a forwarding stub) until the write-back, so it compares equal as well. The first version (`fill_receiver_unchanged`) took the test before the call; that missed a rebind made INSIDE the call, by the `valueOf` / `Symbol.toPrimitive` of start or end (`a.fill(7, { valueOf() { a = [9]; return 0; } })` rebound `a` to the filled original, node keeps `[9]`), and held the compared bits across a collection point. Only a single-local receiver is rooted; any other receiver emits the bare call.
- Test: wasi probes `array-fill-receiver-reassign.js` (value, start and end arguments that rebind a small array and a 1.2M pre-sized one, including a rebind to another array, to itself and from a closure the argument calls; a module global, a closure-captured local and plain locals that are not reassigned and still receive the grown head; compared with node) and `array-fill-coercion-callbacks.js` (the same through `valueOf` / `Symbol.toPrimitive` on start and end; both coercions rebinding; a callback that throws; a module global and a captured local; a literal and a property receiver; compared with node).
- Same-kind audit: the other growing mutators that write a head back, `unshift` and `splice` (the generic arms of `lower_array_method.rs`, `ArrayUnshift` and `ArraySplice` in `expr/arrays_finds.rs` and `expr/instance_misc1.rs`), have the same write-back, and it is upstream's (present in upstream `main` at `c39e81fe1`, the #6229 fix), not the fork's. Not changed, and not run (by inspection only). The HIR variants read the receiver after the arguments, so they are consistent; the generic `lower_array_method` arms evaluate the receiver first and can still overwrite an assignment made by an argument (`a.unshift((a = [9], 0))`).
- Upstream: not cherry-picked. Depends on: P80. PR-BG, a candidate for upstream PerryTS/perry.

### P83 (this commit) fix(perry): key the build caches on PERRY_WASM_SJLJ_DEMOTE
- Area / platform: `COMPILE_ENV_VARS` in `crates/perry/src/commands/compile/compile_env.rs` / all hosts (the variable changes the wasm32 module only).
- Problem: `PERRY_WASM_SJLJ_DEMOTE=0` (P56's before/after switch, read in `perry-codegen/src/inprocess/sjlj_demote.rs`) was not part of the object-cache or completed-build-cache fingerprints, so a build with it flipped could reuse the other setting's objects or output.
- Root cause: P56 added the read without registering it; the audit `compile_env::tests::codegen_env_vars_are_build_cache_inputs` (every `PERRY_*` read in the compiler's crates must be keyed or excluded with a reason) reported exactly this one name, but it is not part of the CI jobs that run on the fork.
- Fix: the name is added to `COMPILE_ENV_VARS` (sorted position). The audit now passes and reports no other unregistered read: the fork added no other `PERRY_*` read to the compile path that is missing.
- Test: the existing audit (`cargo test -p perry --bin perry compile_env`; it failed with `unregistered compiler env reads: ["PERRY_WASM_SJLJ_DEMOTE"]` before and passes after) and `build_cache` unit tests. No new test: the audit is the mechanism that makes the list complete.
- Upstream: not cherry-picked (the pass is fork-only). Depends on: P56. PR-BH.
- Merge of upstream `647b60de8` (2026-10-20): kept. Upstream `c39e81fe1` touched `compile_env.rs`; the `COMPILE_ENV_VARS` entry is intact and the audit's inputs are unchanged.

### P84 (this commit) fix(runtime): hand a native Error super() the refreshed receiver after its init ran user code
- Area / platform: `init_error_family_receiver` in `object/class_registry/construct/site.rs` (reached from `js_class_value_super_construct_site`) / all targets; observable under a moving (copying nursery) collection.
- Problem: a derived class whose heritage is a native Error read at run time (`make(Base) { return class E extends Base { constructor(m, o) { super(m, o); ... } } }`) could continue its constructor on a stale `this` when `super()`'s message ToString or `options.cause` getter allocated enough to run an evacuating collection.
- Root cause: `init_error_family_receiver` passed the raw `this` to `js_error_subclass_default_init_with_options` (which roots it internally and so survives the collection) and then returned `Some(this)`, the pre-collection address. Both callers write that return value over their own refreshed root: `bind` stores `js_ctor_return_override(this, result)` into the `this` slot, and the default derived constructor does `receiver.set_nanbox_f64(result)`.
- Fix: the receiver is rooted in a `RuntimeHandleScope` before the init and the refreshed value is what is returned. Audit of the rest of `site.rs`: the class-entry branch roots `parent` and the receiver before `prepare_super_class_receiver`, and the proxy / reified-builtin branch and `js_fetch_or_value_super` fallback predate the fork (`152fccfa2`, `2bc891313`) and run no user code before their callee takes over, so they were left alone.
- Test: wasi probe `error-subclass-dynamic-gc.js` (message `toString` and `cause` getter each churn 300k allocations under a 1 MB nursery and forced evacuation; compared with node).
- Upstream: not cherry-picked. Depends on: the Error-family receiver init `75654d1a3`. PR-BI.

### P85 (this commit) fix(hir): give each evaluation of a scope its own binding for forward reads of a per-evaluation class declaration
- Area / platform: HIR lowering of class declarations in function bodies (`perry-hir/src/lower_decl/{forward_class_reads.rs,block.rs}`, `lower_decl/body_stmt/gen_capture_scan.rs`, `lower/expr_function.rs`) and the async/generator loop rewrite (`perry-transform/src/generator/per_iteration.rs`) / all targets.
- Problem: P60 made closures lowered before a `class B extends Error` read the evaluated class, but through the template-keyed `js_class_lexical_binding_set/get` table, one slot per class id. A second call of the enclosing function overwrote the slot, so a getter or closure created by the first call (`() => B`) then returned the second call's class (`one.B !== one.direct` after `factory()` ran twice; `instanceof` against the exported class failed for instances of the first one).
- Root cause: the evaluated class lived in process-wide, template-keyed state instead of in the scope that evaluates it. P60 listed it as a limitation (last wins).
- Fix: after a block (and a function-expression body) is lowered, `capture_forward_class_reads` rewrites each `ClassRef(template)` that sits in a closure before the declaration into `LocalGet(binding)` of the declaration's own local, adds that local to the closure's `captures` and `mutable_captures` (so it is boxed), and `redirect_forward_reads_of_fresh_classes` registers the id like a forward-captured `var` (`var_hoisted_ids`) and prepends `PreallocateBoxes`; the declaration's `Let` fills the box. Every invocation of the scope allocates its own box, and the hoisting splits that move function-declaration closures to the front treat that prepend as hoisted. Class declarations that share the first evaluation's binding or live at module level are left alone, as is upstream's use of the get/set table for a reassigned top-level class (`arm_ident.rs`, `expr_assign.rs`). `forward_class_reads.rs` no longer emits `js_class_lexical_binding_*`.
- Fix, follow-ups from review: (1) the rewrite also descends into a fresh class expression other than the declaration's own (`() => class { static base = C }`): its static initializers, computed keys, captured arguments and evaluated parent run in that closure, so a forward read there goes through the binding, keeping the expression's own template. (2) A generator function declaration whose body names a not-yet-lowered per-evaluation class takes the closure route (`nested_generator_references_outer_locals` counts it as an outer local); it used to be a captureless top-level function plus `FuncRef` that could only see the template. Async and plain declarations already lower to closures. (3) In the async/generator transform, `rewrite_written_captures_to_cells` moves the cell of a forward-preallocated binding to the `PreallocateBoxes` position (`let c = [undefined]`) and turns the declaration into a write of `c[0]`, so the snapshot a loop closure takes of the cell (`__periter`) is taken after the iteration's cell exists and the declaration fills that same cell; before, the snapshot copied an uninitialized binding and `read() === C` was false after an `await` in a loop.
- Test: wasi probe `forward-class-binding-reinvoke.js` (getter exported by two invocations, a constructor and static method naming the class, a forward function declaration, a two-level nested closure, a loop body block, a function expression, and a class with static state and captured variables), compared with node; `forward-class-binding-generators.js` (async `for` and `for...of` loops keeping closures across an `await`, async arrows with the declaration before and after the `await`, a generator loop, generator/async/plain function declarations in a scope evaluated twice, fresh class expressions reading the class in a static initializer, a computed key and `extends`, and a factory re-entered three deep before the first declaration runs); `forward-class-binding.js` keeps covering the single-invocation shapes.
- Limitations: a method body of a class (class methods live in `hir.classes`, not as inline closures) that names a later per-evaluation class declaration is not redirected and still reads the template; two same-named class declarations in sibling blocks of ONE function (`for (...) { const r = () => C; class C {} } for (...) { const r = () => C; class C {} }`) share name resolution of the function-wide class registry, so the forward read of the second `C` resolves to the first one's template and binding (the open upstream test `class_member_var_captures::sibling_same_named_class_bindings_construct_their_own_class` is the same defect; the probe keeps one class name per function); a plain box, not a TDZ box: lowering reads the binding before the declaration (the `ClassIsFirstEvaluation` guard of capture registration), where a TDZ box threw `Cannot access 'Cluster' before initialization` in the Storage build (run 39302728586), so an early read of the class from a closure gives `undefined` rather than a `ReferenceError` (it gave the template before). A forward `new B()` in a closure still constructs the template, as with P60.
- Upstream: not cherry-picked. Depends on: none. PR-BJ, a candidate for upstream Perry.
- Merge of upstream `647b60de8` (2026-10-20): kept. Upstream `32a36fc0c` touches `lower/context_new.rs`; the P85 hunks are intact in the merged result.

### P86 (this commit) feat(codegen): PERRY_WASM_STATIC_RELOC selects static relocation for wasm32
- Area / platform: LLVM TargetMachine creation (`perry-codegen/src/inprocess/optimize_emit.rs`, `reloc_mode_for` in `inprocess.rs`) / wasm32 targets only.
- Problem: the wasm32 modules are emitted with PIC relocation, which routes every global through `__memory_base`/`__table_base` adds and GOT-style imports; a statically linked, non-PIC module needs none of them and is smaller.
- Fix: `reloc_mode_for(effective_target)` returns `RelocMode::Static` only when the target starts with `wasm32` and `PERRY_WASM_STATIC_RELOC=1`, and `PIC` in every other case, so the default and every other target are unchanged. The name is registered in `COMPILE_ENV_VARS` (it changes the object bytes, so it is a build-cache input).
- Test: no dedicated probe: the switch changes no language behavior, so every wasi probe is its test. On a `supa-storage.yml` dispatch the default `extra_env` is `PERRY_TYPED_BODIES=0 PERRY_WASM_STATIC_RELOC=1` and `runtime_opt_level` is `s`; the composite action `supa-wasi-env` exports both to wasi-setup, wasi-linux (all shards, with the 78 probes and the 12 sjlj cells), storage-wasi and the renderers, and the runtime archive key (`perry-wasip1-runtime`) and the Storage module key (`storage-wasi-cache`) include both, so no job reuses an artifact built with other settings. The Storage smoke runs on the shipped, stripped and `wasm-opt -Oz` module and diffs its transcripts with node. Pushes use the compiler defaults (PIC). Fast mode composes with the runtime opt-level override (`ci-build-profile.sh` checks the unit graph with the override), and the `compile_env` audit is in `regressions.sh`.
- Upstream: not cherry-picked. PR-BK, a candidate for upstream PerryTS/perry once its own wasm32 CI runs the probe suite with it.
- Merge of upstream `647b60de8` (2026-10-20): kept. Upstream `c39e81fe1` touched `compile_env.rs`; the `PERRY_WASM_STATIC_RELOC` registration is intact.

### P87 (this commit) test(hir): expect a native-module parent class to be a fresh evaluation over its live parent
- Area / platform: HIR lowering of class expressions (`perry-hir/src/lower/lower_expr/arm_class.rs`) and one HIR lib test / all targets.
- Problem: `native_module_parent_keeps_the_shared_template` failed on upstream main as well as the fork. Upstream `152fccfa2` (follow live constructor and home-object heritage) lowers a native-module parent into `parent_expr`, and `per_evaluation_state` includes `parent_expr.is_some()`, so such a class is always a `ClassExprFresh` with `evaluated_parent`. The `!native_parent` term of `identity_only` (#10623) could therefore never decide anything, and its comment claimed the opposite of what the code does.
- Fix: the test now expects `ClassExprFresh{` with `evaluated_parent:Some(`; the dead `native_parent` binding and guard are removed and the comment states the current routing. No behaviour change: `native_extends` is only set with a syntactic `extends`, which always yields a `parent_expr`.
- Test: the renamed HIR test, plus `test-files/test_gap_10623_implicit_ctor_native_super.cts` compiled and run on Linux, whose output matches node (the implicit-constructor argument forwarding #10623 protected still holds on the fresh path).
- Upstream: not cherry-picked. Depends on: none beyond `152fccfa2`. PR-BL, a candidate for upstream PerryTS/perry (also the `sibling_same_named_class_bindings_construct_their_own_class` helper fix, which is test-only and has no ledger id).

### P88 (this commit) fix(runtime): root fill's receiver, value and end operand across the start and end coercions
- Area / platform: `js_array_fill_range` in `perry-runtime/src/array/concat_reverse.rs` / all targets; the stale pointers are visible under a moving collection (wasm32 has no conservative scan), the length and rebind effects are visible everywhere.
- Problem: `a.fill(v, start, end)` coerces start and then end (ToIntegerOrInfinity), which runs a user `valueOf` / `Symbol.toPrimitive`. The runtime held the raw array pointer, the value and the not-yet-coerced end across those calls, so a callback that allocates enough to run an evacuating collection left `arr`, `value` and `end` stale. It also read the length AFTER the coercions, and a callback that shrank the receiver made the fill write slots past the shrunken length without extending it (`let a = [1, 2, 3]; a.fill(0, { valueOf() { a.length = 0; return 0; } })` left `a` empty, node gives `[0, 0, 0]`).
- Root cause: upstream's. The coercions (`08a588ecca`, `da4f8be7fa`, test262 `fill/return-abrupt-from-start`, `fill/coerced-indexes`) were added on top of a function that had never run user code, and nothing rooted the locals at that point.
- Fix: the receiver (`root_raw_mut_ptr`), the value and the end operand are rooted in a `RuntimeHandleScope` before the first coercion and re-read after the last (the receiver through `clean_arr_ptr_mut`, which also follows the forwarding stub of a receiver the callback grew). The length is read first, before any coercion, as the spec reads LengthOfArrayLike. When the range reaches past the receiver's current length (a callback shrank it) each index goes through the extending store, which is the spec's Set. The typed-array branch (`js_typed_array_fill`, which coerces the same operands) is not changed.
- Test: wasi probes `array-fill-coercion-gc.js` (value object and string, end operand, a literal receiver that only the call holds, a variable receiver and a pre-sized one, each across allocating callbacks that churn 300k objects under a 1 MB nursery with forced evacuation; compared with node) and `array-fill-coercion-callbacks.js` (callbacks that push, shrink or grow the receiver).
- Upstream: not cherry-picked. Depends on: none. PR-BM, a candidate for upstream PerryTS/perry.

## Not for upstream

Every other fork-only non-merge commit is CI, probes, a temporary diagnostic, or a Storage shim. None edits files outside `.github/` (checked with `git show --name-only`). There are 44 such commits, 24 fix/feat commits are the patches above, and the fork has no `test:` commits.

**Fork CI workflow, composite action and driver scripts** (`.github/workflows/supa-storage.yml`, `.github/actions/supa-rust-env`, `.github/supa/*.sh`; Blacksmith runner, sccache, lld, caches). Fork-specific infrastructure for supabase/perry. Merge of upstream `2bbab8aff` (2026-10-18): adapted. Upstream's perry compiles natively only against runtime archives that carry a `.gc-effects` sidecar and routes `undici` to `libperry_ext_undici.a`, so `build-perry` writes the sidecars (`scripts/gc_call_effects/sidecars.sh target-libs/release`), builds `perry-ext-undici`, stages both in `perry-dist` (cache key `perry-dist-*-wasi-gcfx-*`), and `regressions-linux` copies the sidecars with the archives. The `perry-ext-zlib` and `perry-ext-ws` wrapper archives are built and staged the same way (compiled programs that import `zlib` or `ws` link them; cache key `perry-dist-*-wasi-gcfx2-*`), and the wasip1 compile of Storage needs no sidecar (`native_link_set_skipped` covers wasi targets; see P31 and P32). The workflow also gained a `wasi_probe_names` dispatch input (run only the named wasi probes) and `wasi-probes.sh` a `// wasm-env: NAME=VALUE...` marker (variables for the wasm run only); both were written to reproduce P53.
Known and parked: the probes `cbp1` to `cbp4` and `class-iife-base-same-name` are open gaps (see P50). The probe `eh-uncaught` failed on aarch64 Linux from before the merge and is fixed by P54.

**Storage size settings in the dispatch workflow** (`supa-storage.yml` inputs `extra_env` and `runtime_opt_level`, the composite action `supa-wasi-env`, `ci-build-profile.sh`, `scripts/wasi_build_runtime.py`, the "Strip and optimize the module" step). Fork CI only. Dispatches build with `PERRY_TYPED_BODIES=0 PERRY_WASM_STATIC_RELOC=1` and a size-optimized (`s`) wasm32 runtime, then `wasm-tools strip --all` and binaryen 133 `wasm-opt -Oz` with an explicit feature list (not `--all-features`: compact imports are rejected by wasmtime) before the module is validated, packed and smoked; the shipped bytes are the ones the smoke runs. The runtime opt-level is passed to cargo as `--config profile.release.opt-level` and `profile.release.package.perry-runtime.opt-level`, keys that compose with the `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_*` variables of the fast profile. Both inputs and the binaryen version are in the runtime archive, module and renderers cache keys. Pushes keep the compiler defaults. Ported from `supa/size-apply` (five commits on `supa/storage-slim`).

**Storage smoke under supa-host** (`.github/supa/wasi-smoke.sh`, job `storage-wasi-smoke` in `supa-storage.yml`, dispatch input `smoke_baseline_run`; the host source is the orphan branch `supa/ci-supa-host`). The job runs the compiled, stripped Storage module under a wasmtime host with the `supa_net` sockets against a Postgres service, three times (a 100 KB upload, a 5 MiB upload, a 100 KB upload with `PERRY_GC_FORCE_EVACUATE=1 PERRY_GC_VERIFY_EVACUATION=1`), and diffs each smoke transcript with the one node produces from the same Storage checkout (`node-reference` artifact). It reports ready time, RSS, the precompiled (`.cwasm`) size and the precompile time, and fails on any difference, a dead host or a host that never answers `/status`. With `smoke_baseline_run=<run id>` it also runs the `storage-wasi-module` artifact of that run on the same host and runner, so sizes and ready times compare like for like. It runs on `supa/wasip1` pushes and on dispatches with `storage_wasi=true`. The host is `host/` of supabase/supa-wasm at `6186ad065` plus a small patch (`--rw-dir`, `--threads`, `compile`, `.cwasm` loading, exceptions and GC on); supabase/supa-wasm is not reachable from this repository's Actions token, which is why the source is vendored on `supa/ci-supa-host`. It is built from outside the checkout (this repository's `.cargo/config.toml` holds nightly-only flags) and cached by the hash of its sources. Known gaps: the host is a snapshot, not supa-wasm's current head; one measurement per run, and ready times on the shared runner vary by a few hundred milliseconds between runs.

`da99fa8be` `7b9b592a3`

**Fastify lazy schema compilation shim** (`.github/supa/patch-fastify-lazy-schema.cjs`, applied by `shims.sh`; `SUPA_LAZY_SCHEMAS=0` skips it for A/B runs). A Fastify-upstream candidate, written against fastify 5.11.2 and generic: it touches no Storage source. Fastify compiles every route's body/params/querystring/headers validators and response serializers while the routes register; in the wasm cold-start profile (supa-wasm run 39175290098) ajv is 65% of the first request's 2.8 s of CPU and fast-json-stringify 16%, almost all of it from this registration-time compile. The shim wraps the `compile` argument of `compileSchemasForValidation` and `compileSchemasForSerialization` in `lib/validation.js` with a `lazyCompiler` helper, so each slot of the route context (`kSchemaBody`, `kSchemaResponse[status][contentType]`, ...) holds a function that calls the real compiler on its first invocation and delegates to the result, mirroring `validate.errors` onto itself after each call (the only property fastify reads from a validator). Observable differences, none reachable with a valid schema: a schema that fails to compile throws at the first request that needs it (a 500 from that request) instead of from `ready()`, and a failed compile is retried on the next call; ajv properties other than `errors` (`schema`, `schemaEnv`, `source`) are not on `getValidationFunction()`'s result; a custom compiler returning a non-function is no longer detected at startup. Checked under node on a 16-route fastify app (params, query, headers, body, `$ref` shared schemas, per-content-type bodies and responses, 2xx/default responses, async and `{value}`/`{error}` custom validators, route-level and encapsulated compilers, `schemaErrorFormatter`, `getValidationFunction`/`compileValidationSchema`): the responses are identical to the eager build except for the order of a custom compiler's side effects and the bad-schema case above. Not covered: Storage's own eager ajv uses (`routes/s3/router.ts` `registerRoute`, `routes/vector/validation.ts`, `routes/bucket/lifecycle.ts`), which this does not defer.

**Ajv boot shim** (`.github/supa/patch-ajv-boot.cjs`, applied by `shims.sh`; `SUPA_LAZY_AJV=0` (workflow input `ajv: eager`) restores the originals for A/B runs). A Storage-specific shim, no Perry change and no P-id, applied on top of the lazy schema shim. Under Perry an Ajv instance compiles the draft-07 meta-schema on its first `addSchema`/`compile`, and every validator is code generation plus `new Function`; three startup costs remained after the lazy schema shim. `dist/http/routes/s3/router.js` `Router.registerRoute` compiled one validator per S3 route (about 100): each route now gets a validator that adds and compiles its schema on first call (the first registration of a method+url key still wins, and `validate.errors` is mirrored onto the wrapper, the only property the S3 handler reads). `@fastify/ajv-compiler`'s pooled ValidatorCompiler (an Ajv instance, the ajv-formats plugin and an `addSchema` per shared schema) is built on the first compile instead of when the first route context asks for it; the pool key and the standalone `code` option still build eagerly. `validateSchema: false` is set on the three Ajv instances Storage builds at boot, so none compiles the meta-schema to check a schema it is about to compile; no check is lost because the reference run under node in storage-prep (original sources, eager registration of every S3 route, fastify compile of every route, `addSchema` of every shared schema) fails to start when any of those schemas is invalid. Differences from eager compilation, none visible with a valid schema: an invalid schema throws from the first request that needs it instead of from startup, and a validator's other ajv properties (`schema`, `schemaEnv`, `source`) are not on the S3 route wrapper. The smoke covers the error paths that go through these validators (invalid json, wrong type, invalid bucket name, bad query, invalid body, S3 validation failure) and diffs them against node.
`1e1d2ad05`

**Storage package stubs** (`.github/supa/storage-stubs.sh` and `stub-packages.cjs`, applied by `shims.sh`; `SUPA_STORAGE_VARIANT=base` (workflow input `storage_variant: base`) keeps the packages for A/B runs). Local-dev only and NOT an upstream candidate: it removes Storage features, so it is neither a Perry change nor something to propose to Storage. The built Storage's AWS SDK (and `@tus/s3-store`, `aws-sigv4-sign`), `@fastify/swagger`/`swagger-ui`, `pg-boss`, `@fastify/rate-limit` and the vector, iceberg, render and admin route modules become throwing stubs before the compile, which takes about 39% off the wasm module; the S3 object backend, TUS on S3, presigned URLs, vectors, iceberg, the job queue, image rate limiting and `/documentation` are gone from that build. supa-wasm's environment never reaches them (`STORAGE_BACKEND=file`, `PG_QUEUE_ENABLE=false`, `RATE_LIMITER_ENABLED=false`, `IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION_ENABLED=false`, vector and iceberg off), except swagger, which registers unless `EXPOSE_DOCS=false`. The S3 protocol endpoint (`/s3`) is unaffected: it verifies sigv4 itself and reads the SDK only for types and one `instanceof`. storage-prep runs the stubbed Storage under node with `EXPOSE_DOCS=false` and fails unless its smoke transcript matches the unstubbed reference apart from the docs probes; that transcript is the reference of storage-wasi-smoke and storage-linux for the stubbed build.
